extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism; playwrights and historians
extracted.subtask_short: literary criticism of drama and history
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria for drama, comedy, and historical writing as articulated in a 19th-century critical essay on Machiavelli — covering plot, character, style, adaptation, and the historian's task. Suitable for assessing dramatic works, adaptations, and historical interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real object of drama
rubrics_metrics.description: The real object of the drama is the exhibition of human character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every other regulation (acts, meter, etc.) is subordinate to this law. Plays should prioritize scenes and situations that reveal character; the best plots are those that most signally develop character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot selects situations that develop character
rubrics_metrics.description: The situations which most signally develop character form the best plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A skilful plot is one chosen for its power to expose and test character, not merely for cleverness of intrigue or novelty of incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style must be the 'mother tongue of the passions'
rubrics_metrics.description: The mother tongue of the passions is the best style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional authenticity should determine style. Any style may be used when appropriate, but the writer must choose the style that most naturally expresses the passions involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of style to place/time/person
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no style which the drama rejects... It is in the discernment of place, of time, and of person, that the inferior artists fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good dramatists adapt tone, diction, and rhetorical manner to the specific character, setting, and historical moment; failures arise when style is mismatched to character or scene (illustrated by comparing Shakespeare's placements to Dryden or Corneille).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid corruption of genre by mannerism
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, Tragedy is corrupted by eloquence, and Comedy by wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive rhetorical eloquence can undermine tragedy's power; excessive ostentatious wit can corrupt comedy. The critic cites examples where ornamental eloquence or indiscriminate witticism weakens the dramatic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety and variety in characterisation (against making characters alike)
rubrics_metrics.description: No writers have injured the Comedy of England so deeply as Congreve and Sheridan... they made all their characters in their own likeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should be differentiated with delicate touches and varying hues; a dramatist who gives every character the same brilliant manner creates a glare that flattens dramatic life. Use contrast (e.g., Falstaff vs. Mirabel) as a test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of human nature can substitute for plot or wit
rubrics_metrics.description: By the correct and vigorous delineation of human nature, [a play] produces interest without a pleasing or skilful plot, and laughter without the least ambition of wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong, truthful characterization can generate both interest and comedy even when plot construction or overt cleverness is modest — cited in praise of Machiavelli's Mandragola.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation of classical plots to contemporary society
rubrics_metrics.description: He has accommodated the plot to a different state of society, and has very dexterously connected it with the history of his own times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imitating ancient or foreign models, the successful dramatist adjusts incidents and relationships to reflect modern habits and social context, thereby making the material resonate for contemporary audiences (example: Machiavelli's handling of Plautus' Casina).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of dialect/language to character
rubrics_metrics.description: The old Tuscan is the very language for such a being. Its peculiar simplicity gives even to the most forcible reasoning and the most brilliant wit an infantine air... It becomes Nicias incomparably, and renders all his silliness infinitely more silly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting a regional or period language can heighten comic effect and authenticity; language choice should match the character's social and cultural position to amplify the intended impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy should ridicule follies of affection rather than mere fatuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The follies which Moliere ridicules are those of affection, not those of fatuity. Coxcombs and pedants, not absolute simpletons, are his game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comedy targets self-regarding pretension, affectation, and social foibles rather than portraying characters as mere idiots; this yields richer, more humane satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verve and correctness in comic verse
rubrics_metrics.description: The verses with which the Mandragola is interspersed, appear to us to be the most spirited and correct of all that Machiavelli has written in metre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic verse in drama should combine spiritedness with technical correctness in metre and diction; judged both by vivacity and formal competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical writing: distinguish accidental from essential
rubrics_metrics.description: He alone reads history aright who, observing how powerfully circumstances influence the feelings and opinions of men... learns to distinguish what is accidental and transitory in human nature from what is essential and immutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historians should emphasize how circumstances shape behavior and avoid overweighing trivial or anecdotal facts; the goal is to discern enduring traits and causes rather than fixating on curiosities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fixation on unimportant historical minutiae
rubrics_metrics.description: How Philip disposed his troops at Chaeronea... whether Mary blew up Darnley... are in themselves unimportant. The inquiry may amuse us, but the decision leaves us no wiser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical historical inquiry should prioritize explanatory and generalizing insight over mere resolution of entertaining but ultimately inconsequential questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, judicious remark, and spirited reporting in political correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The narratives are clear and agreeably written; the remarks on men and things clever and judicious. The conversations are reported in a spirited and characteristic manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political dispatches and correspondence should combine clarity of narrative, perceptive and balanced commentary, and vivid, characteristic reporting of dialogue and manner — qualities that make such documents both informative and engaging.
